# Analytic approach solving Cardano's formula [S1]

The claim accurately reflects the details provided in the evidence. The evidence explicitly states that 'Ray iso-surface intersection tests at the lowest level are performed using an analytic approach solving Cardano’s formula.' It also confirms the use of a hierarchical grid acceleration structure, a three-level bricking approach, macro-cell sizes of approx. 8^3 voxels, and the propagation of min/max values. Furthermore, the performance metrics (1 fps with 1 node, 22 fps with 32 nodes for Visible Female; 2.2-6.7 fps for LLNL) and the comparison to Wald's kd-tree approach (DeMarle's system being slower but using less memory) are all present in the text.

The evidence explicitly states that for the Visible Female data set on a 32-node cluster, performance increases linearly with the number of nodes (from ~1 fps with 1 node to 22 fps with 32 nodes), and that 'All in between values lie on a almost perfect linear line.' This directly supports the claim of linear scalability with cluster size.

-   Repeat until reaching the leaf level (macro-cells of $8^3$ voxels) or the ray exits the volume [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that the hierarchical grid uses a macro-cell size of approximately 8^3 voxels at the leaves. This confirms that the traversal repeats (recurses) until reaching the leaf level (defined by the macro-cells) or the ray exits the volume.
